head: 53c6156e9aa5bb1a0291bb2ac2a6b23bb8c7bdfd
summary: Widened the Explorer-settings write guards in place (src 6 patterns and rule C 9 patterns, so the 6/9 counts and the rules-parity line are unchanged) to catch the RegistryRights overloads of OpenSubKey, PowerShell's string/cast/flags-string/all-string opens, deletes, reg import, and the Copy/Move/Rename-ItemProperty, New-Item and Clear-Item cmdlets. CreateSubKey rights are deliberately not a marker (measured RegSetValueExW=5, B38 quiet). ExplorerSettingsWriteCorpus.json grew from 63 to 124 rows (B30-B51, W35-W73), with bounded_by, aliases, census and closed_by keys, and 12 harness plants (F49-F51, P34-P35, S51-S57) were added. Rows went in first: with the patterns unchanged exactly 42 ids failed and 82 rows plus the Fact passed. After the pattern edits the whole suite passes (935/935), the bug script exits 0, parity is AGREE, the harness reads CLEAN with 16/16 AS-RECORDED, and RuleCases C-001/C-003/C-004/C-005 are green.

CreateSubKey rights are deliberately not a marker (measured RegSetValueExW=5, B38 quiet). files.why: src entry: 4 of 6 patterns widened (DeleteValue, RegistryRights marker without CreateSubKey, RegDelete|SHDelete prefix, DeleteSubKey/DeleteSubKeyTree); rule C: 7 of 9 widened (ItemProperty verb list, New-Item/Clear-Item/Remove-Item, reg /v and import and delete, DeleteValue, OpenSubKey string/cast/flags-string/rights marker, DeleteSubKey*, RegDelete|SHDelete); both `because` texts rewritten to 'bounded by producer'
xUnit twin of the src entry: the same 4 patterns, byte-equal to the yaml after (?m) is stripped; Fact summary rewritten
61 new rows (B30-B51, W35-W73), _note rewritten, new top-level bounded_by, aliases, census and closed_by (42 ids, pre-fix commit 1105c3f); the corpus answer for O-017 and O-018
doc comments only ('closed' reworded to 'bounded', closed_by mentioned); no code change, the 9/6 asserts still hold
12 plants F49-F51, P34, P35, S51-S57 appended in the SL-091 idiom; the _note row counts and id lists updated (123 rows)
the repro stage's acceptance script, kept unchanged; exits 0 now

obligations.how: C-001: rows B30, B31, B33-B37, B40 (and W43) fire. The src marker in fitness.yaml and the Fact carries RegistryRights\]?(\.|::)(SetValue|WriteKey|FullControl). Fed by the corpus Theory; mutation 4 (marker removed from the Fact) fails exactly B30 B31 B33 B34 B35 B36 B37 B40.
C-002: B32 (ReadKey), B38 (CreateSubKey rights, RegSetValueExW=5) and B41 (QueryValues) are quiet rows that pass; the marker deliberately omits CreateSubKey.

C-003: B42-B50 fire (DeleteValue, DeleteSubKeyTree, DeleteSubKey, RegDeleteValue/KeyValue(W)/Tree, SHDeleteValue); B51 (another value deleted) stays quiet. Single-pattern mutations of DeleteValue, the RegDelete prefix and DeleteSubKey each fail exactly their rows.
C-004: B27, B28, B29 and B39 (FromHandle with a constant name) are pinned as miss and pass.
C-005: W35, W41, W42 (PowerShell :: spelling, -bor, permission check) and W43 (C# in the hook) fire under the widened rule C OpenSubKey pattern.
C-006: W36, W37, W38, W46 (a quoted string as the only second argument, bound as $true) fire through the quoted-argument branch of the rule C OpenSubKey pattern; W55 'True' is the control.
C-007: W39 (cast of 'SetValue') and W40 (all-string OpenBaseKey open with 'FullControl') fire; the M2 flags-string rows W65-W67 fire too.
C-008: W44 (enum ReadKey), W47 ($false), W29 (one-argument read), W68 (read-only flags string) and W73 (all-string ReadKey) are quiet; W55 fires.

C-009: W48 (DeleteValue), W49 (Remove-Item of the key), W50 (DeleteSubKeyTree) and W57 (RegDeleteKeyValueW in the hook) fire; mutations of the DeleteValue, DeleteSubKey and import branches fail W48, W50, W51 and W52 respectively.

C-010: W51, W52 (reg import) and W58 (reg add $adv /v Hidden) fire; W09, W10 (reg add on the path) and W11 (reg delete) keep firing. Mutations removing the /v branch (fails W58) and the import branch (fails W51 W52) confirm they are pinned.
C-011: W45, W53, W54, W56, W59 and, new, W69 and W70 (aliases) pass as miss. W60 (New-Item -Force on the key) is now a fire row, not a miss, per accepted review M1.

C-012: all 63 old rows B01-B29 and W01-W34 keep their verdicts and their `before` under the frozen SL-091 patterns; TheCorpusHolds... passes with exactly 9 window and 6 src patterns; parity line unchanged.

C-013: rows were added first with the patterns untouched; the filtered corpus test then failed exactly 42 ids (B30 B31 B33-B37 B40 B42-B50 W35-W43 W46 W48-W52 W57 W58 W60-W67) and passed 83 tests (82 rows plus the Fact). The ids and pre-fix commit 1105c3f are committed in the corpus's closed_by with the command to repeat the run. The design's 33 is superseded by 42 (33 plus B50 and W60-W67 from accepted M1/M2 and a DeleteSubKey row).

C-014: the xUnit twin passes over today's src; rules-parity prints the unchanged AGREE 18 facts <- 22 twinned entries, 48 patterns; 69 settled; Fitness over one file per corpus row agrees with the corpus on 124/124 with 0 stray hits; the harness over the 16 rows (the 4 old ones plus 12 new) reads CLEAN (91 rules, 225 files, 0 hits) with 16 AS-RECORDED; RuleCases C-001, C-003, C-004, C-005 green.

M1: ItemProperty verbs widened to (Set|New|Remove|Clear|Copy|Move|Rename) in :1124 and :1125; New-Item and Clear-Item added beside Remove-Item inside the :1124 lookaround group (count stays 9). W60 flipped to fire; new fire rows W61 (Clear-Item), W62-W64 (Copy/Move/Rename-ItemProperty); quiet rows W71, W72 (unrelated New-Item and Remove-Item); plant S56 (New-Item) AS-RECORDED quiet/fire; census and bounded_by updated. The class is enumerated in the corpus census under 'registry-provider cmdlets'.

M2: the quoted-name alternative of the rule C OpenSubKey pattern is widened to ['"][^'"\r\n]*\b(SetValue|WriteKey|FullControl)\b[^'"\r\n]*['"]. Fire rows W65 ([RegistryRights]'QueryValues, SetValue'), W66 ('SetValue, QueryValues'), W67 (all-string three-argument open with a flags string); quiet rows W68 ('ReadKey, QueryValues' cast) and W73 (all-string ReadKey); plant S57 AS-RECORDED quiet/fire. Fitness and the corpus test agree on all 124 rows.

m1: the six bare Remove-Item aliases were never added; only full cmdlet names sit in the lookaround. W69 (rm on the key) and W70 (sp $adv -Name Hidden) are pinned as miss rows, and bounded_by.aliases_are_a_known_gap and both `because` texts say aliases are a known gap, as in the RuleCases Remove-Item rule.

m2: the corpus `_note` sentence is rewritten (before = the SL-091 declared patterns, not the code before SL-103), and a top-level closed_by key records the 42 SL-103-closed ids, pre-fix commit 1105c3f, and the command that fails them again. A throwaway script checked every id in closed_by, aliases and census exists with the verdict it states, every closed id has before=quiet/now=fire, and every fire/miss row is named in census.
obligations.not_mutable: closed_by and _note are documentation keys that ExplorerSettingsWriteRuleTests.Corpus() deliberately ignores (it reads only `rows`), so no test can observe them; the census check that would is the waived O-021 (SC-308). Their content was verified at build time against the rows.

tests.note: The before-fix run, rows added and patterns still as at 1105c3f: 125 tests, 42 failed (B30 B31 B33-B37 B40 B42-B50 W35-W43 W46 W48-W52 W57 W58 W60-W67), 83 passed. This is the expected failure that shows the fix is what closes the rows.
After the pattern edits: 157/157 (125 corpus tests incl. the Fact, 18 architecture Facts, parity, FailCriticalErrors).
935/935 (874 + 61 new corpus rows), run twice, the second after the mutation runs.
Exit 0, 'All checks held.' It exited 1 with 20 FAILs before the fix.
rules-parity: AGREE 18 facts <- 22 twinned entries, 48 patterns; 69 settled entries not compared (byte-identical to before).

Real engine entry point on a scratch copy of the tree: clean baseline CLEAN (xunit 18 Facts, 0 hits; fitness 91 rules, 225 files, 0 hits, none unmatched; the one import rule NOT RUN as always); 16 rows, 16 AS-RECORDED, 0 stray hits, exit 0. F51 (RegDelete prefix) and S55 (/v branch), the two texts never run through Fitness before, and S56/S57 read as recorded.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 -Case C-001 (then C-003, C-004, C-005)
tests.note: All four 'All checks held.', exit 0 each.

tests.command: python fit-rows.py (throwaway script in a temp folder, since removed): taad3.fitness.check on a scratch tree with one file per corpus row and the worktree's fitness.yaml
tests.note: rows=124 disagreements=0 stray_hits_outside_rows=0: Fitness and the corpus test agree on every row (xUnit matches per line, Fitness over the file, #326).

tests.command: Mutations through a byte-exact backup/restore driver, one exact replacement each, running the corpus Theory
tests.note: Each mutant failed exactly its rows and each file was restored byte-identical (hash checked): New-Item|Clear-Item removed -> W60 W61; narrower quoted-name branch -> W65 W66 W67; rm alias re-added -> W69; src Fact marker without RegistryRights -> B30 B31 B33-B37 B40; Fact DeleteValue -> B42 B43; Fact RegDelete|SHDelete -> B45-B49; Fact DeleteSubKey -> B44 B50; window /v branch -> W58; window import -> W51 W52; window DeleteSubKey -> W50; window DeleteValue -> W48. 'passed' means the mutants were caught.

deviations: The before-fix failing set is 42 ids, not the design's 33: the 33 plus B50 (DeleteSubKey row I added so the DeleteSubKey alternative is pinned on its own) and W60-W67 (W60 flipped miss to fire, W61-W64 and W65-W67 added) from the accepted review findings M1 and M2. Design said 46 rows; 61 were added: B30-B51, W35-W73 (also quiet controls B51, W68, W71, W72, W73 and miss rows W69, W70).

CreateSubKey is dropped from the rights marker, as the design decided; the issue text and build-check C1 name it, and C1's literal wording is therefore not met for that one word. The Sandbox measured RegSetValueExW returning 5 on such a handle, so B38 is a quiet row.
Review m1 changed the design's alias handling: the six Remove-Item aliases were not added (full cmdlet names only), with rm/sp pinned as miss rows.
The design said ExplorerSettingsWriteRuleTests is unchanged; I edited only its doc comments (the word 'closed' contradicted the 'bounded by producer' wording, #400).
The review-accepted rows and top-level keys use `closed_by` as a top-level key rather than a per-row field; plants.json's _note row counts and id lists were updated by hand to stay true (123 rows).
not_built: Review m3 (waived, SC-308): no assertion in TheCorpusHoldsRows... that the census/aliases ids exist with the stated verdicts. Checked once at build time by a throwaway script instead.
Review m4 (waived, SC-309): no miss rows for rights held in a variable, a `using` alias of RegistryRights, or a split parent/child key path; bounded_by.not_pinned says so.
Review m5 (waived, SC-310): no multi-line plant in the repo's real layout.
.reg file content patterns: Fitness reads UTF-16LE as UTF-8 (risk spike no-go), so W53 and W54 are pinned as miss; the engine change is filed.
No semantic (AST or Roslyn) checker and no new architecture_rules, as the design decided.
follow_ups: If the class reopens, replace regex widening with a spelling-independent check: a PowerShell AST check for tests/window and a symbol-level banned-API check for src (#400).
Make taad_v3 Fitness (backend/taad3/fitness.py content_hits) decode a file starting FF FE or FE FF as UTF-16, then rule C could fire W53/W54 on .reg content.
docs/design/SL-091-hidden-reveal-refuses.md still describes these guards as closed as a class; reword it to 'bounded by producer' when next touched.
reg delete and reg import fire whatever key they name (a conservative false positive on unrelated keys, accepted in the design); revisit if a window script ever needs one.
